A base defense game that is both fast paced and slow paced (because of characters' attack speed). Gameplay needs some more tweaking to make it fun. The first hour was great learning things, especially the sudoku mode, it took me a while to know the number representation for each character. I'm a fan of base/tower defense genre. Looking forward to grumpy gaffer's future updates.

The charming visuals of the graphics have a unique and colorful retro cartoon style. It feels like playing on an old-school movie set, Creative gameplay that manages cables and avoids actors, crew, and other messes is a fun challenge that is addictive, Sense of humor: Many funny and absurd moments made me laugh which is an attraction, Easy to pick up, hard to master with simple controls, but the levels are challenging and require quick strategy. Rating 4.8/5

First and foremost, the shooting mechanics in Grumpy Gaffer are surprisingly solid. While it might not boast the hyper-realistic ballistics of a AAA sniper sim, the gunplay feels responsive and impactful. Headshots are particularly gratifying, often accompanied by a satisfying visual and audio cue that really sells the hit. For an indie title, this level of polish in the core shooting loop is commendable and kept me coming back for more. Beyond just the shooting, the game offers a good mix of tactical opportunities. There's a decent variety of enemies, each requiring a slightly different approach, and the level design often provides multiple angles of attack. This encourages you to think about your positioning and utilize the environment to your advantage, much like in Sniper Elite. Whether I was picking off enemies from a distance with a well-placed sniper shot or engaging in closer-quarters combat with an assault rifle, the game always felt engaging.

“Surprisingly fun and totally addictive!” Grumpy Gaffer took me by surprise. What starts off as a simple concept quickly becomes a really satisfying loop. It's fun, charming, and dangerously easy to lose hours to. Definitely one of those "just one more go" games. Highly recommend if you like quirky indie titles with personality!
